recreation_prompt_markdown: Create a mobile-first browser game called 'Meme Rush Infinite' that looks like a neon futuristic social-media app inside a phone frame. The player begins on a stylish onboarding screen where they choose a username tag and an avatar color, then selects one of two modes: a mode about giving 100 likes to dominate the feed, or a mode about reaching 20 clout points to go viral. After starting, show a vertically scrollable meme feed filled with looping reaction GIF posts, fake usernames, short captions, and comment snippets. Each post should have a heart/like button and support double-tap-to-like on the media. A successful first-time like should increase the score, animate the heart, add a particle burst, play a satisfying sound, and briefly show a banner plus a reaction overlay GIF. Use a sticky top HUD with the player tag, avatar badge, target icon, and score progress. Put a decorative bottom navigation bar to reinforce the app parody. Behind the interface, render subtle animated neon background effects on a canvas so the game feels lively. The gameplay loop should be simple and replayable: scroll, rapidly like unique posts, build hype, and hit the target to trigger a celebratory win screen with a victory sound, big message, and replay button. The tone should be chaotic, meme-heavy, arcade-like, and lighthearted rather than realistic, with strong mobile touch targets and portrait-friendly UI throughout.

identity.title: Meme Rush Infinite
identity.premise: A neon-styled mock social-media arcade game where the player creates a tag, enters a viral mode, and farms engagement by liking meme posts in a scrolling feed.
identity.interaction_model: Mobile-first tap and double-tap interaction inside a faux social feed; players select profile options, choose one of two score-chase modes, then like posts until the target is reached.
identity.objective: Accumulate enough successful likes/clout interactions to meet the selected mode target and trigger the victory screen.
identity.progression: Short-session onboarding into two selectable modes, followed by linear score accumulation with audiovisual feedback until a fixed win threshold is met; replay resets the whole run.
identity.theme: Cyber-social meme culture, influencer parody, and arcadeified mobile engagement.
identity.mood: Playful, flashy, ironic, energetic, and low-stakes.
identity.likely_audience: Casual players, meme-heavy mobile users, and younger players who enjoy short arcade loops and social-media parody aesthetics.
confidence_notes: High confidence that this is a casual clicker-style score chase presented as a social feed.
Medium confidence on exact intended distinction between 'give' and 'get' modes because both currently award one point per liked post.
High confidence that the fantasy is viral engagement rather than deep simulation.

selected_categories.reasoning: The core loop is repeated tapping/double-tapping to increment score with immediate audiovisual reward and a fixed target threshold.
The game is framed as a fake social feed full of posts, comments, and profile identity, even though interaction is limited mostly to likes rather than dialogue.
The presentation imitates a social-app environment with profile setup, feed browsing, and community-style content, but lacks multiplayer or shared-space systems.
The fantasy of building hype, clout, and online presence overlaps with creator-economy/streamer progression, though the game has no economy management depth.
Mechanically it resembles a very simple resource-accumulation tap game, but the resource is likes/clout rather than money and there are no upgrades or scaling systems.

uncertainty_notes: The category universe does not include a direct 'social media simulator' or 'engagement tapper' label, so the best fit is approximate.
Several secondary matches are thematic wrappers rather than strong mechanical matches.
The current implementation is much closer to a clicker than to a deep simulator or tycoon.
